DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 128 s. 2021 DEC 20 2021 ATTY. ROMMEL A. GECOLEA City Mayor, Cabuyao, Laguna 2/F Cabuyao Laguna City Hall Rosario Village, Barangay Sala Cabuyao, Laguna Dear Atty. Gecolea: This refers to your letter dated July 9, 2021 requesting from the Department a legal opinion on whether you may register as a One Person Corporation (OPC) under Chapter III, Title XIII of Republic Act No. 11232 or the Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines (RA 11232) in order to appoint a person to manage your family properties. Per your Letter, you and your family own several small parcel of land. Most of your relatives are living abroad, and can only rely on you to manage and administer the parcels of land. Your relatives will, eventually, transfer their lands to you due to sentimental value purposes and to maintain their tradition. You, therefore, intend to register as an OPC. The OPC shall hire an administrator who shall be in charge of administering the properties owned by yourself and your family. You thus seeks the legal opinion of this Department to confirm the legality of your intended action. At the outset, we not have any objection to public officials owning parcels of land, especially those obtained through succession. We are of the opinion that your registration as an OPC may constitute a violation of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code (LGC). We note that Section 90 (a) of the Local Government Code is material to the query at hand. It provides that: "Section 90. Practice of Profession. - (a) All governors, city and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In DILG Opinion Nos. 26 and 30, both series of 2013, this Department confirmed that local chief executives are not required to sell or divest their ownership of shares of stocks in corporations. They are, however, prohibited from taking part in the management of the corporation. DILG Opinion No. 26-2013 provides: "As to your first query, while, as stated above, governors, city and municipal mayors, like you are absolutely prohibited from practicing your profession or engaging in any other occupation during your incumbency, we are of the view, however, that you are not required to dispose, sell or give up your shareholdings in corporations which you already enjoyed prior to your election as such in order to comply with Section 90 of the Local Government Code of 1991. As also mentioned, the rationale behind the prohibition in Section 90 of the Local Government Code of 1991 is to ensure that governors, city and municipal mayors extend their undivided attention and thus devote their full time only in discharging their duties and functions being the highest official of the province, city or municipality. Hence, we are of the view that what Section 90 of the Local Government Code of 1991 only requires is a divestment of management of shareholdings in the corporation, not divestment of title/ownership thereto. Divestment of management entails non- attendance to shareholders meeting and other regular functions of a shareholder, while divestment of title/ownership already requires full disposal of share (e.g. through sale) therein." (Emphasis supplied) It bears to emphasize that Section 121 of the Revised Corporation Code states that: "Section 121. Single Stockholder as Director, President. - The single stockholder shall be the sole director and president of the One Person Corporation." As the sole stockholder, therefore, the same person shall likewise be deemed as the OPC's sole director and president, which are management positions in the corporation. In fact, Section 128 of the Revised Corporation Code, the minimum requirement for any action in the OPC shall be through a resolution signed by the single stockholder. In other words, management is an inherent function of the sole stockholder in an OPC. In view of the foregoing, we submit that you cannot register as an OPC without violating Section 90 of the LGC. Even if an administrator is employed to manage your and your family's' parcels of lands, you are still required, under the Revised Corporation Code, to handle the management of your corporation as a director and president. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to the contrary opinion of more authoritative authority/ies. Page 2 of 3

We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: Unde RINGAN retary for Local Government OUSLG/ML1/LLLA-RALLD/kuq cc: Dir. ARIEL O. IGLESIA Regional Director, DILG Region IV-A 3/F Andenson Building 1 National Highway, Parian City of Calamba, Laguna Page 3 of 3
